summary: As of November 11, 2026, junk-bond spreads are 3.30 percentage points and are down 0.10 percentage points over five trading days. Investment-grade spreads are down 0.03 percentage points over those same five trading days. The CCC-minus-BB gap is 11.37 percentage points. Of the 0.03 percentage-point move in the all-in junk yield, 0.10 was the credit spread and 0.07 was Treasury rates. The 10-year yield is 4.98 percent as of November 10, 2026 and the 30-year is 5.35 percent as of November 10, 2026, a gap of 0.37 percentage points. Brent is 95.41 dollars a barrel as of November 12, 2026 (-2.93 percent over five trading days), and the curve is backwardation. The 5-year inflation breakeven is 2.31 percent as of November 12, 2026, up 0.01 percentage points over five observations. The 10-year real yield is 2.78 percent as of November 10, 2026. The broad dollar index is 121.88 as of November 6, 2026, +0.43 index points over 20 observations. VIX is 17.49 as of November 11, 2026. The Fed balance sheet is 6.76 trillion dollars as of November 11, 2026, up 3 billion dollars over the latest four weekly observations. Reserve balances are 2.96 trillion dollars as of November 11, 2026, down 62 billion dollars over the latest four weekly observations. Overnight reverse repo is 0.25 billion dollars as of November 12, 2026, up 0.125 billion over the latest four observations.
